extracted.intended_audience: members of Congress, congressional staff, policy makers, journalists, and the general public following the Purdue Pharma/Opioid hearings
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional hearing focused on Purdue Pharma, the Sackler family, and corporate responsibility for the opioid epidemic; includes witness testimony, questioning, and documentary evidence cited by members. The document surfaces normative standards used by lawmakers to evaluate corporate conduct and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability for corporate owners and executives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sacklers, not just Purdue, need to be held accountable. There should be repercussion and consequence for the family's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated statements that family members who controlled or directed the company must face consequences (financial restitution, criminal liability, or other repercussions). Example quote: 'The Sacklers, not just Purdue, the Sacklers need to be held accountable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and refusal to allow cover-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Powerful actors must not be allowed to 'cover up the facts, avoid accountability,' or create protected businesses that conceal wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair and members emphasize that permitting concealment is 'not justice' and 'offensive and wrong.' Implies requirement for full disclosure of internal documents and truthful testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful, non-misleading marketing and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing, promotional materials, and labels must not falsely minimize risks (e.g., addiction, tolerance, withdrawal) or claim lesser addictiveness without evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to Purdue's 2007 guilty plea for illegally misbranding OxyContin as 'less addictive, less subject to abuse...' and to specific ads and materials that 'downplayed the risk of the addiction.' Anti-pattern: promotional pieces that instruct 'be careful not to change the perception of physicians toward oxycodone' when that perception understates risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid incentivizing overprescribing through sales compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not reward employees for selling more drugs or direct sales reps to target highest-prescribing doctors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal documents showed sales reps were directed to target highest prescribers and that employees were 'rewarding employees for selling more drugs.' 'Evolve to Excellence' and other programs that rank / reward high-volume prescribers are cited as problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not prioritize profit-maximization over patient safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate decisions must not be driven by attempts to 'pull as much money and profit' from a product when that endangers public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members repeatedly characterize post-penalty behavior as efforts to 'turbo charge sales' and extract as much profit as possible before liabilities catch up—this is presented as morally obscene and a failure of corporate duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility and proper corporate governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards must not function as de facto CEOs in ways that evade responsibility; boards that control operations bear responsibility for harmful corporate practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony references the board 'serving as the de facto CEO' and members noting that family board members 'had control of the operations' and therefore cannot plausibly disclaim knowledge or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exploitation of patient assistance programs to prolong opioid use
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient savings cards and similar programs should not be used as tools to keep patients on opioids longer or to manipulate adherence for profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee cites that patient savings cards 'were consistently tracked and evaluated because Purdue knew these cards were a powerful way to keep patients on opioids longer.' Use of such programs as retention tools is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid targeting vulnerable populations (e.g., seniors, Medicare patients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing strategies should not single out vulnerable groups such as elderly patients or those on Medicare/Medicaid to expand sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal documents stated targeting 'patients over the age of 65' and a 'geriatric strategy' are cited as efforts to grow OxyContin use among seniors—presented as unethical and dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: No manipulation or undue influence over accrediting bodies and clinical guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not fund, influence, or steer accrediting organizations' guidance (e.g., The Joint Commission) in ways that downplay risks or promote increased prescribing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members ask whether Purdue funded Joint Commission research/guides and note a Joint Commission pain-management guide 'sponsored by Purdue' that downplayed addiction concerns—implying funding disclosures and firewalls are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical use of imagery and patient portrayals in promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing should not rely on staged photographs or fabricated 'patients' to humanize and sell a product while misrepresenting clinical effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony notes sales reps provided 'staged photographs featuring fake patients to humanize the sale'—an example of deceptive marketing practices to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceptive statements to physicians (e.g., about potency or safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must correct misconceptions (such as claims that oxycodone is weaker than morphine) rather than exploit them for earlier, broader prescribing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email excerpts show executives chose not to correct the misconception that oxycodone is weaker than morphine and instead used that perception to expand noncancer pain prescribing. Anti-pattern: 'no plans to correct the misconception.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit prescriber-ranking systems that incentivize unsafe prescribing
rubrics_metrics.description: Using metrics like 'value deciles' or ranking prescribers based on access to federal programs to reward high-volume or high-dose prescribing is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Evolve to Excellence' program used prescriber ranking and rewarded doctors who were high-volume Medicare prescribers—cited as an actionable mechanism that increased dangerous prescribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial restitution to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits derived from harmful conduct should be returned to victims or used for remediation; lawmakers question why profits should not be recovered for distribution to families harmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members compare audits of Sackler profits (~$12 billion) to forfeitures in other drug cases and press whether every dollar should be returned to victims—constitutes a standard of full financial remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue criminal or civil liability where warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where evidence shows deliberate deception, companies and responsible individuals should face appropriate criminal or civil sanctions rather than only corporate pleas that leave owners untouched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members express outrage that Purdue's corporate plea left family members 'unscathed' and say justice requires pursuing individuals when conduct merits it (example: comparing to El Chapo forfeiture and life sentence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame addiction as a disease and avoid stigmatizing patients
rubrics_metrics.description: Public officials and companies should acknowledge addiction as a disease and avoid rhetoric that criminalizes or blames people with substance use disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several members press witnesses to agree 'addiction is a disease' and condemn prior family emails that described abusers as 'criminals'—policy implication: avoid stigmatizing language and focus on treatment/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full cooperation with investigations and production of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Executives and companies must respond fully to committee requests for information (e.g., funding records, internal emails) and not obstruct oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple members request that witnesses and company produce information (e.g., Joint Commission funding amounts) and emphasize committee follow-up; evasive 'I don't know' answers are criticized as unacceptable.
